- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or neutral, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days), especially if sentiment was bullish; cap forecast at 10-15% above recent peak.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to correct; reduce forecast slope or add downward bias in second half.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5-10% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates in bearish sentiment periods; add 2-5% buffer if sentiment <0.33 for 3+ days.
- If sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model overreacts; reduce forecast by 3-8% to avoid “sentiment-driven overcorrection.”
